intro.title: Basic Sentence Structure
intro.explanation: Learn the fundamental particles and sentence patterns that form the backbone of Japanese.

items.title: Noun は～ (Noun wa〜)
items.explanation: Used to mark the topic of a sentence; 'as for', 'speaking of'.
items.structure: Noun + は

examples.japanese: 私は日本の料理が好きです。
examples.english: As for me, I like Japanese cuisine.

examples.japanese: 彼は英語が上手です。
examples.english: As for him, he is good at English.

examples.japanese: この本は面白いです。
examples.english: As for this book, it's interesting.

items.title: Noun を〜 (Noun wo〜)
items.explanation: Indicates the direct object of a verb.
items.structure: Noun + を + Verb

examples.japanese: 私は本を読みます。
examples.english: I read a book.

examples.japanese: 彼はケーキを食べました。
examples.english: He ate a cake.

examples.japanese: 母はコーヒーを飲むのが好きです。
examples.english: My mother likes to drink coffee.

items.title: Noun も〜 (Noun mo~)
items.explanation: Indicates that the action or state is the same for multiple items or people; 'also', 'as well'.
items.structure: Noun + も

examples.japanese: 私も日本語を勉強しています。
examples.english: I am also studying Japanese.

examples.japanese: 彼もケーキが好きです。
examples.english: He also likes cake.

examples.japanese: 東京も大阪も観光スポットがたくさんあります。
examples.english: There are many tourist spots in both Tokyo and Osaka.

items.title: ～の (〜no)
items.explanation: Express possession, apposition, or description using 'of' or ''s'.
items.structure: Noun1 + の + Noun2, (Adjective/Clause) + の (nominalized), etc.

examples.japanese: これは私の鞄です。
examples.english: This is my bag.

examples.japanese: 彼女は赤いバッグを持っています。
examples.english: She has a red bag.

examples.japanese: 彼はきれいな部屋があります。
examples.english: He has a clean room.

items.title: ～が (〜ga)
items.explanation: Particle indicating the subject of a sentence or expressing 'but'.
items.structure: Noun + が / い-Adjective + が / な-Adjective + が / Verb + が

examples.japanese: 私が学生です。
examples.english: I am a student.

examples.japanese: このりんごが美味しい。
examples.english: This apple is delicious.

examples.japanese: 彼は頭がいいが、性格が悪い。
examples.english: He is smart but has a bad personality.

intro.title: Existence and Location
intro.explanation: Express what exists and where things are located using あります and います.

items.title: ～あります (〜arimasu)
items.explanation: Indicate possession or existence of inanimate objects; 'there is', 'there are'.
items.structure: Object + が + あります

examples.japanese: 教室に机があります。
examples.english: There is a desk in the classroom.

examples.japanese: この公園にたくさんの花があります。
examples.english: There are many flowers in this park.

examples.japanese: 駅の近くにコンビニがあります。
examples.english: There is a convenience store near the station.

items.title: ～（場所）に～があります (〜basho ni 〜 ga arimasu)
items.explanation: Express the existence or presence of something in a place.
items.structure: Place + に + Object/Thing + が + あります

examples.japanese: 図書館にたくさんの本があります。
examples.english: There are many books in the library.

examples.japanese: 公園に池があります。
examples.english: There is a pond in the park.

examples.japanese: 駅の前にコンビニがあります。
examples.english: There is a convenience store in front of the station.

items.title: Noun に～ (Noun ni～)
items.explanation: Express a specific direction, target or purpose; 'to', 'toward', 'for'.
items.structure: Noun + に

examples.japanese: 彼女にプレゼントをあげました。
examples.english: I gave a present to her.

examples.japanese: 日本に行きます。
examples.english: I am going to Japan.

examples.japanese: 6時に集合しましょう。
examples.english: Let's meet at 6 o'clock.

intro.title: Particles for Direction and Means
intro.explanation: Learn particles that express direction, location of action, and means.

items.title: Nounで～ (Noun de ~)
items.explanation: Indicate a place or means for an action or situation; 'at, in, on', 'using', or 'by means of'.
items.structure: Noun + で

examples.japanese: 図書館で勉強します。
examples.english: I study at the library.

examples.japanese: バスで学校に行きます。
examples.english: I go to school by bus.

examples.japanese: 鉛筆で書きました。
examples.english: I wrote it using a pencil.

items.title: Noun に 行きます (Noun ni ikimasu)
items.explanation: Used to express going to a location.
items.structure: Noun + に + 行きます

examples.japanese: 学校に行きます。
examples.english: I will go to school.

examples.japanese: 明日、スーパーに行きます。
examples.english: I will go to the supermarket tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 週末に映画館に行きます。
examples.english: I will go to the movie theater on the weekend.

items.title: Noun に 来ます (Noun ni kimasu)
items.explanation: Used to express coming to a place.
items.structure: Noun + に + 来ます (kimasu)

examples.japanese: 友達が私の家に来ます。
examples.english: My friend will come to my house.

examples.japanese: 今晩、父が駅に迎えに来ます。
examples.english: Tonight, my father will come to pick me up at the station.

examples.japanese: 明日、先生が学校に来ます。
examples.english: Tomorrow, the teacher will come to school.

items.title: Noun に 帰ります (Noun ni kaerimasu)
items.explanation: Express going back or returning to a place: 'to return to', 'to go back to'.
items.structure: Noun + に + 帰ります

examples.japanese: 夏休みが終わったら、学校に帰ります。
examples.english: When summer vacation ends, I'll go back to school.

examples.japanese: 買い物を終えたら、家に帰ります。
examples.english: After finishing shopping, I will go back home.

examples.japanese: 今週末、実家に帰ります。
examples.english: I'm going back to my parents' home this weekend.

items.title: Noun に 戻ります (Noun ni modorimasu)
items.explanation: Expresses the action of returning to a previous state, place, or condition.
items.structure: Noun + に + 戻ります

examples.japanese: 冷蔵庫に入れると、溶けたアイスクリームは固体に戻ります。
examples.english: When put in the refrigerator, the melted ice cream returns to its solid state.

examples.japanese: 休暇が終わったら、仕事に戻ります。
examples.english: When the vacation ends, I will return to work.

examples.japanese: リモートワークが終わった後、元のオフィスに戻ります。
examples.english: After remote work is over, we will return to our original office.

intro.title: Particles for Range and Listing
intro.explanation: Express ranges with から/まで and list items with と, や, など.

items.title: Noun から Noun まで (Noun kara Noun made)
items.explanation: Expresses a range; 'from...to', 'between...and'.
items.structure: Noun1 + から + Noun2 + まで

examples.japanese: 朝9時から午後5時まで働きます。
examples.english: I work from 9 AM to 5 PM.

examples.japanese: 東京から大阪まで電車で行く。
examples.english: I will go by train from Tokyo to Osaka.

examples.japanese: 地下鉄は午前6時から深夜まで運行しています。
examples.english: The subway runs from 6 AM until midnight.

items.title: Noun と～ (Noun to～)
items.explanation: Express 'with', 'and' or 'together with' when connecting nouns.
items.structure: Noun1 + と + Noun2

examples.japanese: リンゴとバナナを買いました。
examples.english: I bought apples and bananas.

examples.japanese: 友達と映画を見に行きます。
examples.english: I will go to watch a movie with my friend.

examples.japanese: 父と母と一緒に旅行しました。
examples.english: I traveled together with my father and mother.

items.title: Noun や Noun など～ (Noun ya Noun nado)
items.explanation: Lists items or examples but not exhaustively; 'such as', 'like', 'and so on'.
items.structure: Noun1 + や + Noun2 + など

examples.japanese: 彼は野菜や果物などを食べるのが好きです。
examples.english: He likes to eat things like vegetables and fruits.

examples.japanese: 日本の都市や東京、大阪などに行きたいです。
examples.english: I want to go to Japanese cities such as Tokyo, Osaka, and so on.

examples.japanese: 彼女は猫や犬など動物が好きです。
examples.english: She likes animals like cats, dogs, and so on.

items.title: Noun か Noun か～ (Noun ka Noun ka～)
items.explanation: Expresses choice or alternatives; 'either', 'or'.
items.structure: Noun1 + か + Noun2 + か～

examples.japanese: 今日、映画を見るか、散歩するかどちらにしますか？
examples.english: Will we watch a movie or go for a walk today?

examples.japanese: コーヒーか紅茶か、一つだけ選んでください。
examples.english: Please choose only one, either coffee or tea.

examples.japanese: 電車かバスを使って、学校に行くつもりです。
examples.english: I plan to go to school using either the train or the bus.

intro.title: い-Adjective Patterns
intro.explanation: Learn how い-adjectives connect to verbs and change form.

items.title: い-Adjective く + Verb (i-Adjective + ku + Verb)
items.explanation: Used to connect an い-adjective to a verb, modifying the verb (adverbial usage).
items.structure: い-Adjective (remove い) + く + Verb

examples.japanese: 彼は速く走りました。
examples.english: He ran quickly.

examples.japanese: この料理は美味しく食べました。
examples.english: I enjoyed eating this dish.

examples.japanese: 彼女は優しく話します。
examples.english: She speaks kindly.

items.title: い-Adjective く します (i-Adjective ku shimasu)
items.explanation: Use an い-adjective to express 'to make' or 'to become'.
items.structure: い-Adjective (remove い) + くします

examples.japanese: 部屋を明るくします。
examples.english: I will make the room brighter.

examples.japanese: 友達の気分を楽しくします。
examples.english: I will make my friend’s mood more pleasant.

examples.japanese: 仕事が簡単になるように、やり方を早くします。
examples.english: I will make the way of doing things faster so that the work becomes easier.

items.title: い-Adjective: Negative Polite Form
items.explanation: Change an い-adjective into a polite negative form with ～くないです (or ～くありません).
items.structure: い-Adjective (remove い) + くないです

examples.japanese: このピザは美味しくないです。
examples.english: This pizza is not delicious.

examples.japanese: この部屋は広くないです。
examples.english: This room is not spacious.

examples.japanese: 彼の意見は面白くないです。
examples.english: His opinion is not interesting.

items.title: い-Adjective て (i-Adjective + te~)
items.explanation: Used to connect two or more い-adjectives to describe something.
items.structure: い-Adjective (remove い) + くて + い-Adjective

examples.japanese: このリンゴは甘くて美味しいです。
examples.english: This apple is sweet and delicious.

examples.japanese: 彼女は優しくてかわいいです。
examples.english: She is kind and cute.

examples.japanese: 映画は面白くて感動的でした。
examples.english: The movie was interesting and moving.

intro.title: な-Adjective Patterns
intro.explanation: Learn how な-adjectives connect to verbs and express change.

items.title: な-Adjective に + Verb
items.explanation: Turn a な-adjective into an adverb by adding に.
items.structure: な-Adjective (remove な) + に + Verb

examples.japanese: 彼は静かに話す。
examples.english: He speaks quietly.

examples.japanese: 部屋をきれいに掃除した。
examples.english: I cleaned the room neatly.

examples.japanese: 彼女は元気に働いています。
examples.english: She works energetically.

items.title: な-Adjective で～ (na-Adjective de~)
items.explanation: Usage of で to connect or add information with a な-adjective.
items.structure: な-Adjective + で

examples.japanese: 彼は綺麗で優しい女性が好きです。
examples.english: He likes women who are beautiful and kind.

examples.japanese: この料理は健康的で、元気な気分になります。
examples.english: This dish is healthy and makes you feel energetic.

examples.japanese: 彼は静かで落ち着いた環境で仕事をしたい。
examples.english: He wants to work in a quiet and calm environment.

items.title: な-Adjective に します (na-Adjective ni shimasu)
items.explanation: Expressing a decision or preference with a な-adjective.
items.structure: な-Adjective + に + します

examples.japanese: 静かにします。
examples.english: I will be quiet.

examples.japanese: 部屋をきれいにします。
examples.english: I will make the room clean.

examples.japanese: 明日の会議は簡単にします。
examples.english: I will make tomorrow’s meeting simple.

items.title: な-Adjective に なります (na-Adjective ni narimasu)
items.explanation: Express a change or transformation into a state described by the な-adjective.
items.structure: な-Adjective (remove な) + に + なります

examples.japanese: この部屋は静かになります。
examples.english: This room becomes quiet.

examples.japanese: 彼女はきれいになります。
examples.english: She becomes beautiful.

examples.japanese: 彼は元気になります。
examples.english: He becomes energetic.

intro.title: The て-form
intro.explanation: The て-form is one of the most versatile verb forms in Japanese, used for requests, ongoing actions, and connecting sentences.

items.title: Verb て～ (Verb + te～)
items.explanation: A verb conjugation that connects actions or states.
items.structure: Verb (Group 1) - Replace last syllable with 〜て, Verb (Group 2) - Replace 'る' with 〜て, Verb (Group 3) - する becomes して, くる becomes きて

examples.japanese: コーヒーを飲んで、出かけます。
examples.english: After drinking coffee, I will go out.

examples.japanese: 買い物をして、家に帰りましょう。
examples.english: Let's go shopping and then go home.

examples.japanese: 宿題をして、寝ます。
examples.english: After doing my homework, I will sleep.

items.title: Verb て ください (Verb-te kudasai)
items.explanation: A request or command; 'please do'.
items.structure: Verb-て form + ください

examples.japanese: ドアを開けてください。
examples.english: Please open the door.

examples.japanese: 電話番号を教えてください。
examples.english: Please tell me your phone number.

examples.japanese: ゆっくり話してください。
examples.english: Please speak slowly.

items.title: Verb ないで ください (〜naide kudasai)
items.explanation: Used to make a polite request for someone not to do something; 'please don't'.
items.structure: Verb-ない-form + で ください

examples.japanese: タバコを吸わないでください。
examples.english: Please don't smoke.

examples.japanese: ここで走らないでください。
examples.english: Please don't run here.

examples.japanese: 大きな声で話さないでください。
examples.english: Please don't speak loudly.

items.title: Verb て います (Verb te imasu)
items.explanation: Express ongoing action or state; 'is doing', 'is doing (continuous)', 'has been doing'.
items.structure: Verb て-form + います

examples.japanese: 彼女は今ピアノを弾いています。
examples.english: She is playing the piano now.

examples.japanese: 私たちは日本語を勉強しています。
examples.english: We are studying Japanese.

examples.japanese: 彼は映画を見ています。
examples.english: He is watching a movie.

items.title: ～て います (～te imasu)
items.explanation: Expresses the present continuous or ongoing action; 'to be doing', 'currently doing'.
items.structure: Verb て-form + います

examples.japanese: 今、音楽を聞いています。
examples.english: I am listening to music right now.

examples.japanese: 父は新聞を読んでいます。
examples.english: My father is reading a newspaper.

examples.japanese: 彼女は英語を勉強しています。
examples.english: She is studying English.

modules.name: N5 Grammar 8: Verb Forms - Suggestions & Invitations

intro.title: Suggestions and Invitations
intro.explanation: Learn how to make suggestions, invitations, and proposals in Japanese.

items.title: Verb ましょう (mashou)
items.explanation: Making a suggestion or invitation; 'let's' or 'shall we'.
items.structure: Verb (ます-stem) + ましょう

examples.japanese: 一緒に映画を見ましょう。
examples.english: Let's watch a movie together.

examples.japanese: 散歩しましょう。
examples.english: Let's take a walk.

examples.japanese: 今晩、食事に行きましょう。
examples.english: Let's go out for dinner tonight.

items.title: Verb ましょうか。 (〜mashou ka.)
items.explanation: Used to make a polite suggestion or offer help; 'shall we', 'should we', 'do you want me to'.
items.structure: Verb (ます-stem) + ましょうか

examples.japanese: 一緒に映画を見に行きましょうか。
examples.english: Shall we go see a movie together?

examples.japanese: コーヒーをもう一杯飲みましょうか。
examples.english: Should we have another cup of coffee?

examples.japanese: あなたの荷物を持ちましょうか。
examples.english: Do you want me to carry your luggage?

items.title: Verb ませんか。 (Verb-masenka)
items.explanation: An invitation or suggestion; 'won't you', 'why don't you', 'shall we'.
items.structure: Verb (ます-form) + ませんか

examples.japanese: 一緒に映画を見ませんか。
examples.english: Won't you watch a movie together with me?

examples.japanese: 明日のパーティーに参加しませんか。
examples.english: Why don't you join tomorrow's party?

examples.japanese: 週末にピクニックに行きませんか。
examples.english: Shall we go for a picnic on the weekend?

intro.title: Expressing Want and Ability
intro.explanation: Express desires and abilities using たい, ほしい, and できます.

items.title: Verb たいです (taidesu)
items.explanation: Express desire or want to do something; 'I want to', 'I would like to'.
items.structure: る-Verb: Remove る and add たいです, う-Verb: Replace the final verb character with the ～い form and add たいです, Exception: する becomes したいです

examples.japanese: 私は寿司を食べたいです。
examples.english: I want to eat sushi.

examples.japanese: 彼は日本に行きたいです。
examples.english: He wants to go to Japan.

examples.japanese: 彼女は英語を勉強したいです。
examples.english: She wants to study English.

items.title: Noun がほしいです (〜ga hoshii desu)
items.explanation: Express a desire or wanting something; 'I want', 'I would like'.
items.structure: Noun + が + ほしいです

examples.japanese: 新しい車がほしいです。
examples.english: I want a new car.

examples.japanese: コーヒーがほしいです。
examples.english: I would like some coffee.

examples.japanese: 彼女は花がほしいです。
examples.english: She wants flowers.

items.title: Noun が できます (Noun ga dekimasu)
items.explanation: Express the ability to do something.
items.structure: Noun + が + できます

examples.japanese: 英語ができます。
examples.english: I can speak English.

examples.japanese: 料理ができます。
examples.english: I can cook.

examples.japanese: 彼は泳ぎができます。
examples.english: He can swim.

items.title: Verb る こと が できます (ru koto ga dekimasu)
items.explanation: Express the potential form, or the ability to do something.
items.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ことができます

examples.japanese: この問題を解くことができます。
examples.english: I can solve this problem.

examples.japanese: 彼は英語を話すことができます。
examples.english: He can speak English.

examples.japanese: 私は高い所に登ることができません。
examples.english: I can't climb to high places.

items.title: Verb る こと ができる (ru koto ga dekiru)
items.explanation: Expresses the potential form; 'can', 'be able to', 'is possible'.
items.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + ことができる

examples.japanese: この問題を解くことができる？
examples.english: Can you solve this problem?

examples.japanese: 彼は泳ぐことができます。
examples.english: He can swim.

examples.japanese: 日本に行くことができて、とても嬉しいです。
examples.english: I'm very happy that I can go to Japan.

intro.title: Time and Sequence
intro.explanation: Express the order of events and timing using before, after, and when.

items.title: Verb た あとで (ta ato de)
items.explanation: Indicates an action that takes place after another action.
items.structure: Verb-た form + あとで

examples.japanese: 宿題をしたあとで、テレビを見ました。
examples.english: After doing my homework, I watched TV.

examples.japanese: 朝ごはんを食べたあとで、歯を磨きます。
examples.english: After eating breakfast, I brush my teeth.

examples.japanese: 仕事が終わったあとで、ジムに行く予定です。
examples.english: After finishing work, I plan to go to the gym.

items.title: Noun の あとで (Noun no atode)
items.explanation: Expresses the order of events; 'after', 'later than'.
items.structure: Noun + の + あとで

examples.japanese: 朝ご飯のあとで、歯を磨きます。
examples.english: After breakfast, I brush my teeth.

examples.japanese: 映画のあとで、レストランで夕食を食べました。
examples.english: After the movie, we ate dinner at a restaurant.

examples.japanese: 会議のあとで、上司と話し合います。
examples.english: I will discuss with my boss after the meeting.

items.title: Verb る 前に (ru mae ni)
items.explanation: Used to express 'before' in a sense of an action must be done before another action or event.
items.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + 前に

examples.japanese: 出かける前に、部屋を掃除してください。
examples.english: Please clean the room before leaving.

examples.japanese: 寝る前に、歯を磨きます。
examples.english: I brush my teeth before going to bed.

examples.japanese: 雨が降る前に、洗濯物を取り込むこと。
examples.english: Take in the laundry before it rains.

items.title: Noun の 前に (Noun no mae ni)
items.explanation: Used to describe a location or position 'in front of' a noun.
items.structure: Noun + の + 前に

examples.japanese: 駅の前にコンビニがあります。
examples.english: There is a convenience store in front of the station.

examples.japanese: 家の前に車を止めてください。
examples.english: Please park the car in front of the house.

examples.japanese: 私の前に彼が立っていました。
examples.english: He was standing in front of me.

items.title: Verb てから～ (〜te kara)
items.explanation: Express a sequence of actions or events; 'after', 'since', 'once'.
items.structure: Verb-て形 + から

examples.japanese: 宿題をしてから、テレビを見ました。
examples.english: I watched TV after doing my homework.

examples.japanese: 食べてから、歯を磨きましょう。
examples.english: Let's brush our teeth after eating.

examples.japanese: 仕事が終わってから、友達と飲みに行きます。
examples.english: I will go drinking with my friends after work is done.

intro.title: Giving and Receiving
intro.explanation: Japanese has distinct verbs for giving and receiving depending on the social relationship.

items.title: ～に あげます (〜 ni agemasu)
items.explanation: Used to express giving something to someone; 'give', 'offer'.
items.structure: Receiver + に + Object + を + あげます

examples.japanese: 私は友達に本をあげました。
examples.english: I gave a book to my friend.

examples.japanese: 彼にプレゼントをあげましょう。
examples.english: Let's give him a present.

examples.japanese: 先生に花をあげます。
examples.english: I will give flowers to the teacher.

items.title: ～に もらいます (〜ni moraimasu)
items.explanation: To receive something or some action from someone; 'to get', 'to receive'.
items.structure: Giver + に + Verb-te form + もらいます / Giver + に + Object + を + もらいます

examples.japanese: 友達にプレゼントをもらいました。
examples.english: I received a gift from my friend.

examples.japanese: 先生にアドバイスをもらいました。
examples.english: I got advice from my teacher.

examples.japanese: おばあさんに手紙を書いてもらいました。
examples.english: I had my grandmother write a letter for me.

items.title: ～から もらいます (〜kara moraimasu)
items.explanation: To receive something or get someone to do something.
items.structure: Noun + から + (Verb-て form) + もらいます

examples.japanese: 友達からプレゼントをもらいました。
examples.english: I received a present from my friend.

examples.japanese: 先生に宿題を渡してもらいました。
examples.english: I had the teacher hand me the homework.

examples.japanese: お母さんに料理を作ってもらいました。
examples.english: I got my mom to cook for me.

items.title: ～が 私に くれます (〜ga watashi ni kuremasu)
items.explanation: Used to express that someone gives a gift or favor to 'me'; 'someone gives me'.
items.structure: Person + が + (Thing or Action) + 私に + くれます

examples.japanese: 彼がプレゼントを私にくれました。
examples.english: He gave me a present.

examples.japanese: 友達が宿題を手伝って私にくれました。
examples.english: My friend helped me with my homework.

examples.japanese: お母さんがお弁当を作って私にくれました。
examples.english: My mom made me a lunch box.

intro.title: Making Comparisons
intro.explanation: Learn to compare two or more things and express superlatives.

items.title: A は B より～ (A wa B yori～)
items.explanation: Express a comparison between A and B; 'A is more/less than B'.
items.structure: A は B より + Adjective

examples.japanese: このジュースはあのジュースより甘いです。
examples.english: This juice is sweeter than that juice.

examples.japanese: 夏は冬より暑いです。
examples.english: Summer is hotter than winter.

examples.japanese: 彼女は私より速く走ります。
examples.english: She runs faster than me.

items.title: A より B のほうが～ (A yori B no hou ga ～)
items.explanation: Used to compare two items; 'B is more ～ than A'.
items.structure: A + より + B + のほうが + Adjective

examples.japanese: ピザよりハンバーガーのほうが美味しい。
examples.english: Hamburgers are more delicious than pizza.

examples.japanese: 夏より冬のほうが寒い。
examples.english: Winter is colder than summer.

examples.japanese: ここよりそこのほうが静かです。
examples.english: There is quieter than here.

items.title: Aと Bと どちら～ (A to B to dochira~)
items.explanation: Used to ask which of two alternatives is preferred or to compare two things
items.structure: Aと Bと どちら + Verb/Adjective/Noun

examples.japanese: りんごとみかんとどちらが好きですか。
examples.english: Which do you like, apples or oranges?

examples.japanese: 電車とバスとどちらで行くべきですか。
examples.english: Should I go by train or bus?

examples.japanese: 赤いワンピースと青いワンピースとどちらが似合うと思いますか。
examples.english: Which do you think suits me better, the red dress or the blue dress?

items.title: AとBと どっち〜 (A to B to docchi〜)
items.explanation: Asking which one; 'which', 'A or B'.
items.structure: AとBと どっち + Verb, AかBか どっち + Verb

examples.japanese: コーヒーと紅茶とどっちが好き？
examples.english: Which do you like, coffee or tea?

examples.japanese: 映画と音楽とどっちを楽しむ？
examples.english: Which do you enjoy, movies or music?

examples.japanese: 赤いシャツと青いシャツとどっちを買う？
examples.english: Which one will you buy, the red shirt or the blue shirt?

items.title: A が いちばん～ (A ga ichiban～)
items.explanation: Express the superlative degree; 'the most', 'the best', 'the least'.
items.structure: Noun + が + いちばん + Adjective/Verb

examples.japanese: この中で、寿司が一番好きです。
examples.english: Of all these, I like sushi the most.

examples.japanese: 彼女はクラスで一番速く泳げます。
examples.english: She can swim the fastest in the class.

examples.japanese: この町では、この公園が一番きれいです。
examples.english: In this town, this park is the most beautiful.

modules.name: N5 Grammar 13: Question Words - What & Who

intro.title: Question Words: What and Who
intro.explanation: Learn to ask about things and people using なに, だれ, and their variations.

items.title: なに～ (nani~)
items.explanation: Asking about 'what' or 'which' in Japanese
items.structure: Verb + なに, い-Adjective + なに, な-Adjective + なに, Noun + なに

examples.japanese: これはなにですか。
examples.english: What is this?

examples.japanese: あの人はなにをしているのですか？
examples.english: What is that person doing?

examples.japanese: なにが好きですか？
examples.english: What do you like?

items.title: なん～ (nan~)
items.explanation: Used to form interrogative questions and emphasize the question word for 'what', 'how'.
items.structure: なん + Counter / なん + Verb / なん + Adjective

examples.japanese: あなたはなん歳ですか？
examples.english: How old are you?

examples.japanese: これはなんですか？
examples.english: What is this?

examples.japanese: 彼はなんで来ましたか？
examples.english: Why did he come?

items.title: だれ～ (dare～)
items.explanation: Asking 'who' in a sentence, used to inquire about someone's identity or to clarify who is being referred to.
items.structure: だれ + appropriate particle (が, は or を)

examples.japanese: だれがその本を買いましたか。
examples.english: Who bought that book?

examples.japanese: だれを待っていますか。
examples.english: Whom are you waiting for?

examples.japanese: だれがそのリンゴを食べましたか。
examples.english: Who ate that apple?

items.title: どなた～ (donata～)
items.explanation: A polite way to ask 'who', used for asking about someone's identity or when seeking information about an unknown person.
items.structure: どなた

examples.japanese: すみません、どなたが山田さんですか？
examples.english: Excuse me, who is Mr. Yamada?

examples.japanese: どなたも知っている有名な俳優です。
examples.english: He is a famous actor whom everyone knows.

examples.japanese: 明日のパーティーにはどなたが来ますか？
examples.english: Who is coming to the party tomorrow?

items.title: なんで～ (nande～)
items.explanation: Asking the reason or cause; 'why', 'how come'.
items.structure: なんで + [phrase or sentence]

examples.japanese: なんで遅れたの？
examples.english: Why were you late?

examples.japanese: なんでこの部屋はこんなに汚いの？
examples.english: Why is this room so dirty?

examples.japanese: なんで彼女は怒っているの？
examples.english: Why is she angry?

modules.name: N5 Grammar 14: Question Words - Where & Which

intro.title: Question Words: Where and Which
intro.explanation: Ask about locations and make selections using どこ, どの, どれ, and どちら.

items.title: どこ～ (doko～)
items.explanation: Express 'where', used with question words for asking about locations.
items.structure: どこ + question particle

examples.japanese: 駅はどこですか？
examples.english: Where is the station?

examples.japanese: どこで映画を見ましたか？
examples.english: Where did you watch the movie?

examples.japanese: どこに住んでいますか？
examples.english: Where do you live?

items.title: どちら～ (dochira～)
items.explanation: Used to ask about two choices or options.
items.structure: どちら + が/を + verb, どちら + が/を + adjective, どちら + が/を + noun

examples.japanese: この二つのリンゴ、どちらが美味しいですか？
examples.english: Which of these two apples is delicious?

examples.japanese: どちらのドレスを着たいですか？
examples.english: Which dress would you like to wear?

examples.japanese: この二つの町、どちらに行きたいですか？
examples.english: Which of these two towns do you want to go to?

items.title: どの Noun (dono Noun)
items.explanation: Expresses 'which'; used to ask about specific items within a group.
items.structure: どの + Noun

examples.japanese: どの本が一番面白いですか。
examples.english: Which book is the most interesting?

examples.japanese: どの服を着たいですか。
examples.english: Which clothes do you want to wear?

examples.japanese: どの色が好きですか。
examples.english: Which color do you like?

items.title: どんな Noun (donna)
items.explanation: Used to ask or describe 'what kind' or 'what type' of something.
items.structure: どんな + Noun

examples.japanese: どんな音楽が好きですか？
examples.english: What kind of music do you like?

examples.japanese: 彼女はどんな映画が好きだと思う？
examples.english: What kind of movies do you think she likes?

examples.japanese: どんな本が一番面白いですか？
examples.english: What kind of books are the most interesting?

items.title: いくつ～ (ikutsu~)
items.explanation: Used to express 'how many' or ask for the number of something.
items.structure: いくつ + Noun (optional)

examples.japanese: リンゴはいくつありますか？
examples.english: How many apples are there?

examples.japanese: いくつかの問題を解決しなければなりません。
examples.english: I have to solve several problems.

examples.japanese: あなたはいくつの言語を話せますか？
examples.english: How many languages can you speak?

intro.title: Asking How
intro.explanation: Learn different ways to ask 'how' and make suggestions.

items.title: ～どうですか。 (〜dou desu ka.)
items.explanation: Asking for opinions or suggestions; 'how about', 'what do you think of'.
items.structure: Noun + は/が + どうですか / Verb-casual + の + どうですか / い-Adjective + どうですか / な-Adjective + な + どうですか

examples.japanese: この映画はどうですか？
examples.english: How about this movie? / What do you think of this movie?

examples.japanese: 晩ご飯に寿司を食べるのはどうですか？
examples.english: How about eating sushi for dinner?

examples.japanese: この部屋は広いと思いますが、どうですか？
examples.english: I think this room is spacious, what do you think?

items.title: ～どう しますか。 (～dou shimasu ka.)
items.explanation: Asking for someone's opinion or decision; 'what will you do?', 'how will you handle it?'.
items.structure: Situation + どうしますか

examples.japanese: 雨が降っているので、どうしますか？
examples.english: It's raining, so what will you do?

examples.japanese: この問題について、どうしますか？
examples.english: What are you going to do about this issue?

examples.japanese: 彼が来なかったら、どうしますか？
examples.english: If he doesn't come, what will you do?

items.title: どうやって～ (douyatte～)
items.explanation: Ask 'how' something is done or how to do something.
items.structure: どうやって + Verb-casual

examples.japanese: どうやってお寿司を作りますか？
examples.english: How do you make sushi?

examples.japanese: どうやって日本語を勉強しましたか？
examples.english: How did you study Japanese?

examples.japanese: どうやってこの問題を解決しますか？
examples.english: How do you solve this problem?

items.title: ～いかがですか。 (〜ikaga desu ka.)
items.explanation: A polite way to ask someone's thoughts, opinions, or preferences; 'how about', 'how is'.
items.structure: Noun + は + いかがですか / (Verb-て form + は) いかがですか

examples.japanese: お茶はいかがですか？
examples.english: How about some tea?

examples.japanese: このドレスはいかがですか？
examples.english: How about this dress?

examples.japanese: ケーキを食べてはいかがですか？
examples.english: How about eating some cake?

items.title: ～なんと 言いますか。 (〜nan to iimasu ka.)
items.explanation: Asking how something is called or referred to; 'how do you say'
items.structure: Noun + は/が + なんと言いますか

examples.japanese: この花はなんと言いますか。
examples.english: How do you say this flower?

examples.japanese: この料理はなんと言いますか。
examples.english: What do you call this dish?

examples.japanese: 日本でこれはなんと言いますか。
examples.english: How do you say this in Japanese?

items.title: ～どう 言いますか。 (〜dou iimasu ka.)
items.explanation: Asking for the way to say something; 'how do you say'.
items.structure: Word/Phrase + は [language]でどう言いますか / Word/Phrase + をどう言いますか

examples.japanese: 「ありがとう」は英語でどう言いますか。
examples.english: How do you say 'thank you' in English?

examples.japanese: この言葉を日本語でどう言いますか。
examples.english: How do you say this word in Japanese?

examples.japanese: 「すみません」はフランス語でどう言いますか。
examples.english: How do you say 'excuse me' in French?

intro.title: Indefinite Pronouns: Someone, Something, Somewhere
intro.explanation: Express indefinite references using か-compounds.

items.title: なにか～ (nanika～)
items.explanation: Indicates 'something' or 'some kind of'.
items.structure: なにか + Noun

examples.japanese: なにか飲み物を持ってきてください。
examples.english: Please bring some kind of drink.

examples.japanese: なにか質問があれば、遠慮なく聞いてください。
examples.english: If you have any questions, please feel free to ask.

examples.japanese: 彼女はなにかプレゼントを持っている。
examples.english: She has some kind of present.

items.title: だれか〜 (dareka〜)
items.explanation: Indicates 'someone' or something done or possessed by 'someone'.
items.structure: だれか + Verb, だれか + Adjective, だれか + Noun

examples.japanese: だれかがドアをノックしました。
examples.english: Someone knocked on the door.

examples.japanese: だれかが私の傘を盗みました。
examples.english: Someone stole my umbrella.

examples.japanese: だれか助けてください。
examples.english: Someone, please help.

items.title: どこか～ (dokoka～)
items.explanation: Expresses 'somewhere', used when the specific location is unknown or uncertain.
items.structure: どこか + (Particle, if needed) + Verb/Noun/Adjective

examples.japanese: どこかで財布をなくしました。
examples.english: I lost my wallet somewhere.

examples.japanese: 今日はどこかに行きたいです。
examples.english: I want to go somewhere today.

examples.japanese: どこか安いレストランがありますか？
examples.english: Is there a cheap restaurant somewhere?

items.title: いつか～ (itsuka～)
items.explanation: Indicates an unspecified point in time; 'someday', 'one day', 'at some point'.
items.structure: いつか + sentence

examples.japanese: いつか日本に行きたいです。
examples.english: I want to go to Japan someday.

examples.japanese: 彼はいつか有名な作家になるでしょう。
examples.english: He will become a famous writer someday.

examples.japanese: いつかあの山を登りたいと思っています。
examples.english: I think I want to climb that mountain someday.

modules.name: N5 Grammar 17: Indefinite Pronouns - Every & None

intro.title: Every and None
intro.explanation: Express universal and negative indefinite references.

items.title: なんでも～ (nandemo～)
items.explanation: Means 'any', 'anything', 'anyone'.
items.structure: なんでも + Verb / なんでも + Adjective / なんでも + Noun

examples.japanese: なんでも食べられるから、何を頼んでも大丈夫です。
examples.english: I can eat anything, so it's okay to order whatever you want.

examples.japanese: なんでもよければ、この本をおすすめします。
examples.english: If you're okay with anything, I recommend this book.

examples.japanese: なんでもできるスタッフを探しています。
examples.english: We are looking for a staff member who can do anything.

items.title: だれでも～ (dare demo～)
items.explanation: Used to express 'anyone' or 'everyone'; 'no matter who'.
items.structure: だれでも + Verb/Adjective/Noun

examples.japanese: だれでもこのゲームができます。
examples.english: Anyone can play this game.

examples.japanese: だれでも疲れることがあります。
examples.english: Everyone gets tired sometimes.

examples.japanese: だれでも無料でこのイベントに参加できます。
examples.english: Anyone can participate in this event for free.

items.title: どこでも～ (dokodemo～)
items.explanation: Express 'anywhere' or 'everywhere' in Japanese.
items.structure: Simply use the word どこでも in the sentence as an adverb to indicate 'anywhere' or 'everywhere'.

examples.japanese: どこでも好きな場所で勉強できます。
examples.english: You can study anywhere you like.

examples.japanese: このノートパソコンは便利なので、どこでもインターネットが使えます。
examples.english: This laptop is convenient, so you can use the internet anywhere.

examples.japanese: 彼はどこでも寝ることができます。
examples.english: He can sleep anywhere.

items.title: いつでも～ (itsudemo～)
items.explanation: Expresses 'anytime', 'always', or 'whenever'.
items.structure: いつでも + (Verb)

examples.japanese: いつでも遊びに来てください。
examples.english: Please come to play anytime.

examples.japanese: 彼女はいつでも笑顔です。
examples.english: She is always smiling.

examples.japanese: いつでも電話で連絡できます。
examples.english: You can contact me by phone anytime.

items.title: どれでも～ (dore demo～)
items.explanation: Indicates 'any' or 'whichever' when referring to multiple items.
items.structure: どれ + でも

examples.japanese: どれでもいいですか？
examples.english: Is any choice okay?

examples.japanese: どれでも選んでください。
examples.english: Please choose whichever you like.

examples.japanese: どれでもおいしいです。
examples.english: All of them are delicious.

intro.title: Nobody, Nothing, Nowhere
intro.explanation: Express negative indefinites - nobody, nothing, and nowhere.

items.title: なにも～ないです (nani mo~nai desu)
items.explanation: Used to express 'not any' or 'nothing' in a negative sentence.
items.structure: なにも + Verb-negative

examples.japanese: 彼はなにも言わなかったです。
examples.english: He didn't say anything.

examples.japanese: 私はなにも食べないです。
examples.english: I don't eat anything.

examples.japanese: 彼女はなにも持っていないです。
examples.english: She doesn't have anything.

items.title: なにも～ません (nanimo~masen)
items.explanation: Used to express 'not anything', 'nothing'.
items.structure: なにも + Verb-ます form + ません

examples.japanese: 昨日はなにも食べませんでした。
examples.english: I didn't eat anything yesterday.

examples.japanese: 彼はなにも話しません。
examples.english: He doesn't say anything.

examples.japanese: この部屋ではなにも見えません。
examples.english: I cannot see anything in this room.

items.title: だれも～ないです (dare mo ~ nai desu)
items.explanation: Express 'nobody' or 'no one' in a negative sentence.
items.structure: だれも + Verb-negative form (ないです), だれも + い-Adjective-negative form (ないです), だれも + な-Adjective-negative form (じゃないです)

examples.japanese: だれも知らないです。
examples.english: Nobody knows.

examples.japanese: だれも来ないです。
examples.english: Nobody is coming.

examples.japanese: 彼女はだれも好きじゃないです。
examples.english: She doesn't like anyone.

items.title: だれも～ません (daremo ~masen)
items.explanation: Express 'nobody' or 'no one' in negative sentences.
items.structure: だれも + Verb-negative (ません)

examples.japanese: だれも秘密を知りません。
examples.english: No one knows the secret.

examples.japanese: だれもその質問に答えませんでした。
examples.english: Nobody answered that question.

examples.japanese: だれも彼を助けてあげません。
examples.english: Nobody will help him.

intro.title: Nowhere Patterns
intro.explanation: Multiple ways to express 'nowhere' depending on the particle used.

items.title: どこにも + Verb + ないです (doko ni mo + Verb + nai desu)
items.explanation: Express that an action cannot be performed anywhere or something cannot be found anywhere.
items.structure: どこにも + Verb in ない-form + です

examples.japanese: どこにも傘が売ってないです。
examples.english: Umbrellas are not sold anywhere.

examples.japanese: 彼はどこにも見つけられないです。
examples.english: He cannot be found anywhere.

examples.japanese: どこにも勉強できる場所がないです。
examples.english: There is no place to study anywhere.

items.title: どこにも + Verb + ません (doko ni mo + Verb + masen)
items.explanation: Express 'not anywhere' or 'nowhere' with a negative verb.
items.structure: どこにも + Verb-negative

examples.japanese: どこにもあの猫がいません。
examples.english: The cat is not anywhere.

examples.japanese: どこにもお金を置いていません。
examples.english: I didn't put the money anywhere.

examples.japanese: この町にはどこにも美味しいラーメン屋がありません。
examples.english: There are no delicious ramen shops anywhere in this town.

items.title: どこへも Verb ないです (doko e mo + Verb + nai desu)
items.explanation: Express that an action doesn't take place anywhere; 'nowhere', 'not anywhere'.
items.structure: どこへも + Verb in negative form (ないです)

examples.japanese: 今週末どこへも行かないです。
examples.english: I'm not going anywhere this weekend.

examples.japanese: 彼女はどこへも買い物に行きませんでした。
examples.english: She didn't go shopping anywhere.

examples.japanese: スーパーはどこへも売らないです。
examples.english: It's not sold at any supermarket.

items.title: どこへも Verb ません (doko e mo + Verb + masen)
items.explanation: Nowhere; Not to any place
items.structure: どこへも + Verb-negative

examples.japanese: 今日はどこへも行きません。
examples.english: I won't go anywhere today.

examples.japanese: 彼はどこへも走りませんでした。
examples.english: He didn't run anywhere.

examples.japanese: どこへも買い物に行きませんでした。
examples.english: I didn't go shopping anywhere.

items.title: どこも Verb ないです (dokomo + Verb + naidesu)
items.explanation: Express that something cannot be found anywhere or in any place; 'nowhere', 'in no place'.
items.structure: どこも + Verb-negative

examples.japanese: どこもうちわがないです。
examples.english: I can't find fans anywhere.

examples.japanese: この町ではどこも美味しいラーメンがないです。
examples.english: There are no delicious ramen shops anywhere in this town.

examples.japanese: どこも駐車場がないです。
examples.english: There is no parking anywhere.

items.title: どこも Verb ません (dokomo + Verb + masen)
items.explanation: Express that 'nowhere' meets the verb action; 'nowhere does/can'.
items.structure: どこも + Verb-ます form + ません

examples.japanese: どこも静かじゃありません。
examples.english: Nowhere is quiet.

examples.japanese: どこもその本を売っていません。
examples.english: Nowhere sells that book.

examples.japanese: この地域では、どこもインターネットに接続できません。
examples.english: In this area, nowhere can connect to the internet.

intro.title: Conjunctions: Contrast
intro.explanation: Connect contrasting ideas using various 'but' and 'however' expressions.

items.title: A。けれども、～B。(A. Keredomo,~ B.)
items.explanation: Used to express a contrast between two statements. It can be translated as 'but' or 'however'.
items.structure: Statement A + けれども、+ Statement B

examples.japanese: 今日は晴れている。けれども、寒いです。
examples.english: It is sunny today. However, it is cold.

examples.japanese: 彼女はうるさい。けれども、面白いです。
examples.english: She is noisy. But, she is interesting.

examples.japanese: その映画は長かった。けれども、退屈じゃなかった。
examples.english: The movie was long. But, it wasn't boring.

items.title: A。しかし、～B。 (A. Shikashi, ~B.)
items.explanation: Expresses contrast or contradiction between two clauses; 'A, but B', 'A, however B'.
items.structure: Sentence A + しかし + Sentence B.

examples.japanese: 今日は忙しい。しかし、時間があるなら、コーヒーを飲もう。
examples.english: I'm busy today. However, if I have time, let's have coffee.

examples.japanese: その映画は面白かった。しかし、長すぎました。
examples.english: The movie was interesting. But, it was too long.

examples.japanese: 彼は疲れていた。しかし、宿題を終わらせた。
examples.english: He was tired. However, he finished his homework.

items.title: A。でも、～B。(A. Demo, ~B)
items.explanation: Used to express contrast between two statements; 'A, but B', 'A, however B'.
items.structure: Clause A + でも + Clause B

examples.japanese: 昨日は寒かった。でも、今日は暖かいです。
examples.english: Yesterday was cold. But today it's warm.

examples.japanese: 彼は忙しい。でも、友達と遊ぶ時間がある。
examples.english: He is busy. However, he still has time to hang out with friends.

examples.japanese: 試験に合格した。でも、まだ勉強を続けています。
examples.english: I passed the exam. But I'm still continuing to study.

items.title: ～が、～ (〜ga, 〜)
items.explanation: Express a contrast between two sentences; 'but', 'however'.
items.structure: Sentence 1 + が、+ Sentence 2

examples.japanese: デザートは美味しいが、カロリーが高い。
examples.english: The dessert is delicious, but it is high in calories.

examples.japanese: 彼は頭がいいが、少し怠け者だ。
examples.english: He is smart, but a bit lazy.

examples.japanese: 会社は利益を上げたが、従業員の給与は上がらなかった。
examples.english: The company made a profit, however, the employees' salaries did not increase.

items.title: ～けど、～ (〜kedo、～)
items.explanation: Used to connect two clauses; 'but', 'however', 'although'
items.structure: Verb-casual + けど / い-adjective + けど / な-adjective + だけど / Noun + だけど

examples.japanese: 授業に出たけど、まだ宿題をしないといけない。
examples.english: I attended the class, but I still have to do my homework.

examples.japanese: 昨日寒かったけど、今日は暖かいです。
examples.english: Yesterday was cold, but today is warm.

examples.japanese: 彼は親切だけど、ちょっと怖い。
examples.english: He is kind, but a little scary.

items.title: ～けれど、～ (〜keredo、～)
items.explanation: Expresses a contrast or contradiction; 'but', 'however', 'even though'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + けれど / い-Adjective + けれど / な-Adjective + だけれど / Noun + だけれど

examples.japanese: 今日は寒いけれど、散歩に行きます。
examples.english: Even though it's cold today, I'll go for a walk.

examples.japanese: 彼は親切けれど、少し怖いです。
examples.english: He is kind, but a little scary.

examples.japanese: この部屋は狭いけれど、明るいです。
examples.english: This room is small, but it's bright.

intro.title: Conjunctions: Cause and Sequence
intro.explanation: Connect ideas showing cause, result, and sequence.

items.title: ～から、～ (〜kara、～)
items.explanation: Expresses reason or cause; 'because', 'since', 'so'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + から / い-Adjective + から / な-Adjective + だから / Noun + だから

examples.japanese: 明日は試験があるから、今晩勉強しなければなりません。
examples.english: Because I have an exam tomorrow, I must study tonight.

examples.japanese: この部屋は狭いから、もっと大きい部屋を探しています。
examples.english: Since this room is small, I am looking for a bigger one.

examples.japanese: 彼は友達だから、手伝ってくれるでしょう。
examples.english: Since he is my friend, he will probably help me.

items.title: ～からです (〜kara desu)
items.explanation: Express the reason or cause; 'because', 'since', 'due to'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + からです / い-Adjective + からです / な-Adjective + だからです / Noun + だからです

examples.japanese: 寒いからです。コートを着ています。
examples.english: It’s because it’s cold. That’s why I’m wearing a coat.

examples.japanese: この店は安いからです。よく来ます。
examples.english: It’s because this store is cheap. That’s why I come often.

examples.japanese: 彼は親切だからです。みんなに好かれています。
examples.english: It’s because he’s kind. Everyone likes him.

items.title: だから、～ (dakara、～)
items.explanation: Expresses a reason or cause; 'because', 'so', 'therefore'.
items.structure: Noun + だから / な-Adjective + だから

examples.japanese: 雨だから、傘を持って行きましょう。
examples.english: Because it's raining, let's bring an umbrella.

examples.japanese: このケーキは有名だから、みんなが食べたいです。
examples.english: Because this cake is famous, everyone wants to eat it.

examples.japanese: 彼は病気だから、学校に行けません。
examples.english: Because he is sick, he cannot go to school.

items.title: そして、～ (soshite、～)
items.explanation: Used to connect two sentences; 'and then', 'and'.
items.structure: Sentence 1 + そして + Sentence 2

examples.japanese: 朝起きて、そして宿題をしました。
examples.english: I woke up in the morning and then did my homework.

examples.japanese: コーヒーを飲んで、そして新聞を読みました。
examples.english: I drank coffee and then read the newspaper.

examples.japanese: 家を出発しました。そして、駅へ行きました。
examples.english: I left my house and then went to the station.

items.title: それから、～ (sorekara、～)
items.explanation: Meaning 'after that', 'and then' or 'then', indicating sequence of events.
items.structure: Clause 1 + それから + Clause 2

examples.japanese: コーヒーを飲んで、それから家を出ました。
examples.english: I drank coffee, and then I left the house.

examples.japanese: 買い物をして、それから映画を見に行きました。
examples.english: I went shopping, and then I went to watch a movie.

examples.japanese: 彼女は勉強をして、それから寝ました。
examples.english: She studied, and then she went to sleep.

intro.title: Transition Words
intro.explanation: Smooth conversation transitions using 'well then' and 'in that case'.

items.title: A。じゃ、～B。(A. Ja, ~B.)
items.explanation: Indicates a decision or suggestion; 'well then', 'in that case', 'so'.
items.structure: A: Sentence, B: Sentence (A and B can be any sentence type)

examples.japanese: 映画は時間がない。じゃ、また今度行こう。
examples.english: There's no time for a movie. Well then, let's go another time.

examples.japanese: お腹がすいた。じゃ、レストランに行こう。
examples.english: I'm hungry. In that case, let's go to a restaurant.

examples.japanese: 電車が遅れた。じゃ、バスで行こう。
examples.english: The train is late. So, let's go by bus.

items.title: A。それじゃ、～B。(A. Soreja,~B.)
items.explanation: Connect two sentences; 'A, so/in that case, B'
items.structure: Sentence A + 。それじゃ、 + Sentence B

examples.japanese: 今日は休みです。それじゃ、映画を観に行きましょう。
examples.english: Today is a day off. In that case, let's go watch a movie.

examples.japanese: 電気が切れた。それじゃ、ろうそくを使いましょう。
examples.english: The electricity went out. In that case, let's use candles.

examples.japanese: レストランが混んでいます。それじゃ、別の場所で食べましょう。
examples.english: The restaurant is crowded. In that case, let's eat somewhere else.

items.title: A。それでは、～B。(A. Soredewa,~B.)
items.explanation: Express a change in situation; 'then', 'in that case', 'so'.
items.structure: A (Statement) + 。それでは、 + B (Follow-up action or statement)

examples.japanese: 今日は休みだ。それでは、映画を見に行こう。
examples.english: Today is a day off. In that case, let's go see a movie.

examples.japanese: このパンはもう古いです。それでは、捨てましょう。
examples.english: This bread is already old. Then, let's throw it away.

examples.japanese: 雨が降ってきた。それでは、室内で遊ぼう。
examples.english: It started raining. In that case, let's play indoors.

items.title: A。 では、～B。 (A. Dewa, ~B)
items.explanation: Indicates a contrast or comparison between A and B; 'As for A, ~B'.
items.structure: Noun A + では、 + Subject + Predicate B

examples.japanese: 果物では、リンゴが一番好きです。
examples.english: As for fruits, apples are my favorite.

examples.japanese: スポーツでは、サッカーが一番人気です。
examples.english: As for sports, soccer is the most popular.

examples.japanese: 今日の天気では、雨が降りそうです。
examples.english: As for today's weather, it looks like it will rain.

items.title: こちら～ (kochira～)
items.explanation: Refers to a person, place or thing; 'this', 'this one', 'this way', 'here'.
items.structure: こちら / こちら + の + Person/Thing

examples.japanese: こちらは田中さんです。
examples.english: This is Mr./Ms. Tanaka.

examples.japanese: こちらのレストランは美味しいです。
examples.english: This restaurant is delicious.

examples.japanese: こちらへどうぞ。
examples.english: Please come this way.

items.title: そちら～ (sochira～)
items.explanation: Indicates a direction or person in moderate distance; 'that way', 'that person'.
items.structure: そちら [alone] / そちら + の + Noun

examples.japanese: そちらのレストランはどうですか？
examples.english: How is that restaurant over there?

examples.japanese: そちらの方、お名前を教えていただけますか？
examples.english: Could you tell me the name of that person over there?

examples.japanese: そちらに行く途中で駅があります。
examples.english: There is a station on the way to that direction.

intro.title: Frequency and Degree
intro.explanation: Express how often and to what degree things happen.

items.title: いつも～ (itsumo～)
items.explanation: Expressing 'always' or 'usually' in a sentence.
items.structure: いつも + Verb / Adjective / Noun

examples.japanese: 彼はいつも遅刻します。
examples.english: He is always late.

examples.japanese: 私はいつも優しい犬が好きです。
examples.english: I always like gentle dogs.

examples.japanese: 彼女はいつも静かな場所で勉強します。
examples.english: She always studies in a quiet place.

items.title: たいてい～ (taitei～)
items.explanation: Used for expressing 'usually', 'mostly', or 'generally'.
items.structure: たいてい + Verb/い-Adjective/な-Adjective/Noun

examples.japanese: たいてい朝８時に起きます。
examples.english: I usually wake up at 8 o'clock in the morning.

examples.japanese: 彼はたいてい遅刻します。
examples.english: He is usually late.

examples.japanese: この店の商品はたいてい安いです。
examples.english: The items at this store are usually cheap.

items.title: ときどき～ (tokidoki～)
items.explanation: Used to indicate the frequency of an event; 'sometimes', 'occasionally', 'now and then'.
items.structure: ときどき + Verb/Adjective/Noun

examples.japanese: 彼はときどきケーキを作ります。
examples.english: He sometimes makes cakes.

examples.japanese: ときどき雨が降るので、傘を持って行ったほうがいいです。
examples.english: It occasionally rains, so it's better to bring an umbrella.

examples.japanese: 私はときどきこの店で買い物をします。
examples.english: I shop at this store now and then.

items.title: よく～ (yoku ~)
items.explanation: Often used to express 'doing something well' or 'often'.
items.structure: よく + Verb-casual

examples.japanese: 彼はよく勉強します。
examples.english: He studies often.

examples.japanese: 彼女はよく料理を作ります。
examples.english: She often cooks.

examples.japanese: 昔の友達とよく遊んでいました。
examples.english: I used to play a lot with my old friends.

items.title: あまり～ありません (amari ~ arimasen)
items.explanation: Express 'not very', 'not much', or 'not really' when describing a negative state or situation.
items.structure: あまり + Verb-ないform + ありません / あまり + い-Adjective-く ありません / あまり + な-Adjective・Noun じゃありません

examples.japanese: 彼はあまり疲れていません。
examples.english: He is not really tired.

examples.japanese: 彼女はあまり早くないですよ。
examples.english: She is not very fast.

examples.japanese: 私はあまり勉強しないです。
examples.english: I don't study very much.

items.title: あまり～ないです (amari ~ nai desu)
items.explanation: Express 'not really' or 'not very'; used to soften a negative statement.
items.structure: あまり + Verb-ないform + です / あまり + い-Adjective-くない + です / あまり + な-Adjective-じゃない + です

examples.japanese: あまり食べないです。
examples.english: I don't really eat much.

examples.japanese: この映画はあまり面白くないです。
examples.english: This movie is not really interesting.

examples.japanese: 彼はあまり親切じゃないです。
examples.english: He is not very kind.

intro.title: Degree and Approximation
intro.explanation: Express approximate amounts, degrees, and extents.

items.title: ぜんぜん～ (zenzen～)
items.explanation: Used to express 'not at all' or 'completely' in negative sentences.
items.structure: ぜんぜん + [Negative verb/adjective]

examples.japanese: 彼はぜんぜん話さない。
examples.english: He doesn't talk at all.

examples.japanese: この部屋はぜんぜん暗くない。
examples.english: This room is not dark at all.

examples.japanese: 彼女はぜんぜん疲れていない。
examples.english: She is not tired at all.

items.title: だいたい〜 (daitai〜)
items.explanation: Expresses 'roughly', 'approximately', or 'almost'.
items.structure: だいたい + Number/Amount/Percentage

examples.japanese: だいたい１００人がパーティーに参加しました。
examples.english: Approximately 100 people attended the party.

examples.japanese: 彼女はだいたい２時間でその仕事を終えます。
examples.english: She finishes that work in roughly two hours.

examples.japanese: だいたい８０％の生徒が試験に合格しました。
examples.english: About 80% of the students passed the exam.

items.title: ほとんど〜 (hotondo〜)
items.explanation: Used to express 'almost', 'nearly', or 'most'.
items.structure: ほとんど + Verb / ほとんど + Noun

examples.japanese: 彼女はほとんど英語を話せません。
examples.english: She can hardly speak English.

examples.japanese: ほとんどの人がパーティーに出席しました。
examples.english: Most people attended the party.

examples.japanese: 私たちはほとんど勉強しないでテストに合格しました。
examples.english: We passed the test with hardly any studying.

items.title: まあまあ～ (maa maa～)
items.explanation: Expresses something as 'so-so', 'not bad', or 'average'.
items.structure: Used as an adverb or short expression with no special grammar structure.

examples.japanese: 彼の料理の腕前はまあまあです。
examples.english: His cooking skills are so-so.

examples.japanese: 今日の天気はまあまあですね。
examples.english: The weather today is not bad, huh?

examples.japanese: あの映画はまあまあ面白かったです。
examples.english: That movie was somewhat interesting.

items.title: もっと〜 (motto〜)
items.explanation: Expresses 'more' or 'even more' when describing a quantity, frequency, or degree.
items.structure: もっと + Verb / い-Adjective / な-Adjective

examples.japanese: もっと勉強しなければなりません。
examples.english: I have to study more.

examples.japanese: このかばんをもっと大きいサイズに変えたいです。
examples.english: I want to change this bag to a larger size.

examples.japanese: もっと静かな場所で働きたいです。
examples.english: I want to work in a quieter place.

intro.title: Time-Related Expressions
intro.explanation: Express timing, duration, and temporal relationships.

items.title: さっき～ (sakki～)
items.explanation: Refers to a short time ago or just now.
items.structure: さっき + verb / さっき + phrase

examples.japanese: さっき電話がありました。
examples.english: There was a phone call just now.

examples.japanese: さっき部屋を掃除しました。
examples.english: I cleaned the room a short while ago.

examples.japanese: さっき彼に会いました。
examples.english: I met him just now.

items.title: すぐに～ (sugu ni～)
items.explanation: Immediately or right away; used to express promptness or quickness.
items.structure: すぐに + Verb/Adjective

examples.japanese: 友達が来たら、すぐに電話をかけてください。
examples.english: When my friend arrives, please call me right away.

examples.japanese: そのニュースを聞いたら、すぐに会社に行きました。
examples.english: Upon hearing that news, I went to the company immediately.

examples.japanese: 彼女はすぐに泣き出した。
examples.english: She started crying right away.

items.title: もう～ (mou～)
items.explanation: Expresses 'already', 'anymore', or 'soon'.
items.structure: もう + Verb / もう + Adjective / もう + Noun

examples.japanese: もう昼ごはんを食べました。
examples.english: I already ate lunch.

examples.japanese: もうここでは働かない。
examples.english: I won't work here anymore.

examples.japanese: もうすぐ夏休みですね。
examples.english: Summer vacation is coming soon, isn't it?

items.title: もうすぐ〜 (mou sugu~)
items.explanation: Express an action or event happening soon: 'soon', 'in a short while', 'almost'.
items.structure: もうすぐ + Verb (~ます form or 〜る form)

examples.japanese: もうすぐ春が来ます。
examples.english: Spring is coming soon.

examples.japanese: もうすぐ彼女の誕生日です。
examples.english: Her birthday is coming up soon.

examples.japanese: もうすぐ試験が終わる。
examples.english: The exam will be over soon.

items.title: まだ〜 (mada〜)
items.explanation: Indicates something has not yet happened or is still happening; 'still', 'not yet'.
items.structure: まだ + Verb (non-past / negative / te-form), まだ + い-adjective, まだ + な-adjective + じゃない/ではない, まだ + Noun + じゃない/ではない

examples.japanese: 昼ご飯はまだ食べていません。
examples.english: I haven't eaten lunch yet.

examples.japanese: 山田さんはまだ来ていません。
examples.english: Yamada-san has not arrived yet.

examples.japanese: この部屋はまだ暑いです。
examples.english: This room is still hot.

intro.title: Negation Patterns
intro.explanation: Various ways to express 'not yet' and negative states.

items.title: まだ〜ないです (mada 〜 nai desu)
items.explanation: Expresses that something has not happened or been done yet.
items.structure: まだ + Verb-negative + です

examples.japanese: まだ宿題をしていないです。
examples.english: I haven't done my homework yet.

examples.japanese: 彼はまだ来ないです。
examples.english: He hasn't come yet.

examples.japanese: 映画はまだ始まっていないです。
examples.english: The movie hasn't started yet.

items.title: まだ～ません (mada ~masen)
items.explanation: Expresses that something has not happened or been done yet (polite form).
items.structure: まだ + Verb-ます form (negative)

examples.japanese: 昼ご飯をまだ食べていません。
examples.english: I have not eaten lunch yet.

examples.japanese: 宿題がまだ終わっていません。
examples.english: I have not finished my homework yet.

examples.japanese: 東京にはまだ行ったことがありません。
examples.english: I have not been to Tokyo yet.

items.title: ～はたいへんです (〜wa taihen desu)
items.explanation: Express that something is difficult or tough.
items.structure: Noun + はたいへんです

examples.japanese: 漢字を覚えるのはたいへんです。
examples.english: It is difficult to remember kanji.

examples.japanese: この仕事はたいへんです。
examples.english: This job is tough.

examples.japanese: 日本の駅のことを理解するのはたいへんです。
examples.english: Understanding Japanese train stations is difficult.

intro.title: Verb Nominalization and Miscellaneous Patterns
intro.explanation: Turn verbs into nouns and learn additional useful patterns.

items.title: Verb ること～ (〜ru koto)
items.explanation: Express an action or event as a noun; 'the act of', 'doing'.
items.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + こと

examples.japanese: 泳ぐことが大好きです。
examples.english: I love swimming.

examples.japanese: 日本語を勉強することは楽しいです。
examples.english: Studying Japanese is fun.

examples.japanese: 友達と話すことがストレスを軽減します。
examples.english: Talking with friends reduces stress.

items.title: Verb る の～ (Verb + ru + no~)
items.explanation: Used to express the purpose or reason in casual speech, or nominalize the verb with の.
items.structure: Verb (dictionary form) + の (casual)

examples.japanese: 買い物をするために、銀行でお金をおろすの。
examples.english: I'm withdrawing money at the bank so I can go shopping.

examples.japanese: 友達にプレゼントをあげるので、ケーキを焼くの。
examples.english: I'm baking a cake because I'm giving my friend a present.

examples.japanese: ダイエットを始めるので、ジムに入会するの。
examples.english: I’m joining a gym since I'm starting a diet.

items.title: Noun だけ〜 (〜dake)
items.explanation: Indicates 'only', 'just', or 'merely'.
items.structure: Noun + だけ, Verb-casual + だけ, い-Adjective + だけ, な-Adjective-な + だけ

examples.japanese: コーヒーだけ飲んで、帰りました。
examples.english: I only drank coffee and went home.

examples.japanese: この本は二十ページだけ読んだ。
examples.english: I only read twenty pages of this book.

examples.japanese: 彼女はとても速いですが、走るだけでなく、考えるのも速いです。
examples.english: She is very fast, not only at running but also at thinking.

items.title: Noun くらい～ (Noun kurai～)
items.explanation: Express the extent or degree of something; 'about', 'approximately', 'at least'.
items.structure: Noun + くらい

examples.japanese: この本は三百ページくらいあります。
examples.english: This book has about 300 pages.

examples.japanese: 彼の家まで歩いて20分くらいかかります。
examples.english: It takes about 20 minutes to walk to his house.

examples.japanese: 明日は暑くて、30度くらいになるでしょう。
examples.english: Tomorrow will be hot, about 30 degrees.

items.title: Noun ぐらい～ (Noun gurai～)
items.explanation: Express an approximate amount or degree; 'about', 'approximately'.
items.structure: Noun + ぐらい

examples.japanese: 一日中勉強したので、１０時間ぐらい勉強しました。
examples.english: I studied all day, so I studied for about 10 hours.

examples.japanese: この本は１００ページぐらいある。
examples.english: This book has about 100 pages.

examples.japanese: 彼は果物を５個ぐらい食べました。
examples.english: He ate about 5 pieces of fruit.

items.title: Noun ごろ～ (Noun + goro～)
items.explanation: Expresses 'around' or 'about' a certain time or age.
items.structure: Noun + ごろ

examples.japanese: 昼ごろに電話してください。
examples.english: Please call me around noon.

examples.japanese: 彼は10歳ごろに日本に来ました。
examples.english: He came to Japan around the age of 10.

examples.japanese: 午後３時ごろに会いましょう。
examples.english: Let's meet around 3 PM.

items.title: ～とき (〜toki)
items.explanation: Expresses the time when something happens, 'when', 'at the time'.
items.structure: Verb-casual + とき / い-Adjective + とき / な-Adjective + なとき / Noun + のとき

examples.japanese: 公園で遊ぶとき、帽子をかぶりましょう。
examples.english: When playing in the park, let's wear a hat.

examples.japanese: このりんごが赤いとき、食べごろです。
examples.english: This apple is ready to eat when it is red.

examples.japanese: 私が勉強するとき、家族は静かにしてくれます。
examples.english: When I am studying, my family keeps quiet for me.

intro.title: Purpose, Decisions, and Change
intro.explanation: Express purpose of going/coming, making decisions, and changes of state.

items.title: Verb に 行きます (Verb ni ikimasu)
items.explanation: To go (somewhere) in order to do an action.
items.structure: Verb (ます-stem) + に + 行きます

examples.japanese: 公園に遊びに行きます。
examples.english: I will go to the park to play.

examples.japanese: 図書館に勉強しに行きます。
examples.english: I will go to the library to study.

examples.japanese: スーパーに買い物に行きます。
examples.english: I will go to the supermarket to do some shopping.

items.title: Verb に 来ます (Verb ni kimasu)
items.explanation: Expresses the purpose of coming to a place; 'come to (do something)'.
items.structure: Verb (ます-stem) + に + 来ます

examples.japanese: 友達に会いに来ました。
examples.english: I came to meet my friend.

examples.japanese: 映画を見に来ました。
examples.english: I came to watch a movie.

examples.japanese: 先生に質問しに来ました。
examples.english: I came to ask the teacher a question.

items.title: Noun に します (Noun ni shimasu)
items.explanation: Express a choice or decision; 'choose', 'decide on'.
items.structure: Noun + に します

examples.japanese: 今日の昼ご飯は寿司にします。
examples.english: I'll choose sushi for today's lunch.

examples.japanese: この靴を買うか迷っていますが、赤い色の方にします。
examples.english: I was hesitating about which shoes to buy, but I'll go with the red ones.

examples.japanese: 休みの日に何をするか決めた。映画館に行くことにします。
examples.english: I've decided what to do on my day off. I'll go to the movie theater.

items.title: ～たり、～たり します (〜tari, 〜tari shimasu)
items.explanation: Used to list multiple actions or states; 'do things like', 'and'.
items.structure: Verb-casual-past + たり + Verb-casual-past + たり + します

examples.japanese: 休日には、映画を見たり、友達と遊んだりします。
examples.english: On holidays, I do things like watch movies and hang out with friends.

examples.japanese: 彼は歌ったり、踊ったり、ピアノを弾いたりします。
examples.english: He sings, dances, plays the piano, among other things.

examples.japanese: このレストランでは、寿司を食べたり、刺身を食べたりします。
examples.english: At this restaurant, you can eat sushi, sashimi, and so on.

items.title: A は B が〜 (A wa B ga〜)
items.explanation: Indicates that there is something unique or different about A and describes what is special about it.
items.structure: A は (Topic) + B が (Characteristic/Feature) + Description/Action

examples.japanese: 彼女は髪が長いです。
examples.english: What's special about her is that she has long hair.

examples.japanese: このレストランは雰囲気が良いです。
examples.english: What's great about this restaurant is the atmosphere.

examples.japanese: 私は朝ごはんが一番好きです。
examples.english: What I like the most is breakfast.

items.title: Noun に なります (Noun ni narimasu)
items.explanation: Expresses change or becoming something; 'to become', 'to turn into', 'to be'.
items.structure: Noun + に + なります

examples.japanese: 彼は医者になります。
examples.english: He will become a doctor.

examples.japanese: この茶色の葉が赤になります。
examples.english: These brown leaves will turn red.

examples.japanese: 料理が冷めたら、美味しくなくなります。
examples.english: When the dish cools down, it becomes less delicious.
